Aeauen and Earth, & other Creaturer, and laſtly of Man. chap. 1. & 2.
The ſecoud part is of the trangreſlion & falof man, & his caſfingu

The ſignification of the markes here vſed, for
direction of the reader.
The numbers in the argumentes of chapters point to the verſe, where the mat-
ter mentioned beg inneth.
This forme of croſſe ( † ) in the tert, sheweth the beginning of euerie verſe.
The numbers in the inner margent ouer againſt the croſſes, shew the number
of verſes in the ſame chapter.
This marke ſig niſieth that there foloweth an Annotation after the chapter,
vpon the word, or wordes, wherto it is adioyned. The number alſo of the
ſame verſe is prefixed to the Annotation.
Theſe foure prickes :: shew that there is an Annotation in the margent, vpon
that place. And when manie occurre, the firſt anſwereth. to the firſt marcke,
the ſecond to the ſecond, and ſo forth. In like maner the citations of places
in the inner margent, are applied to the authores alleaged.
But when thete be more ſuch marginal annorations, thea may eaſely be ap-
plied, we vſe the lettets of the Alphabete for direction.
This forme of a ſtarre († ) in the text or annotations, pointeth to the explica-
tion of ſome word or wordes, in the margent.
Sometimes we put the Concordance of other Scriptures in the inner mar-
gent of the text.
WVe haue alſo noted in the margent, when the Bookes of holie Scripture (or
partes thereof) are read in the Churches Seruice. For their ſakes, that dciue
to read the ſame, in order ofthe Ferleſiaſtical Office.
